Third, one enters the stage of the right determination (*samyaktva-niyāma*).
Even if one were in a state of regression, [this would not occur].
They are unable to cultivate the roots of various virtues;
this is precisely because they have attained entry into the stage of nature (gotrabhūmi) and are necessarily fixed within that state.
Thus, one knows that the fundamental attainment is accomplished.
Fourth is the arousal of the mind to rescue all sentient beings. Having thus possessed these three practices, [one attains realization].
He perfected great compassion and universally delivered all beings;
having thus fulfilled the four practices.
In future ages, they shall be able to circulate this sutra.

From "In the midst of the five hundred turbid and evil worlds" below,
until the end, he then spoke the mantra, saying:
"May Samantabhadra protect the two bases for the disciples."
This refers to attaining supernatural transformation (*abhijñā-vikurvaṇa*). Regarding "losing the verses and phrases through delusion":
this is not actual delusion; rather, because the patterns and principles of the text are difficult to discern, one may lose them.
When both the words and the meaning are simultaneous,
it is called the *svādhiṣṭhāna-dhāraṇī*. Below this,
from "relying upon" down to "upholding," [the stages are explained].
The second is the instruction on the protective incantation;
the third begins from "World-Honored One, if there be a bodhisattva" and concludes with "may it not be interrupted."
The exhortation for the two [types of persons] to rely upon and uphold [the teachings] follows from the section "If there is a bodhisattva... within the third provisional [classification].
Having exhausted the power of his majestic spiritual authority,
he praised the virtues and capabilities of Samantabhadra,
saying: "If there are those who receive and uphold [this teaching]..."
Having finished, he stroked their heads with his hand.
He raised two who were dependent disciples;
how much more so those who had attained practice and emerged as disciples?
If one merely transcribes the following oneself,
one will experience joy and happiness upon completion;
this clarifies the second basis for the disciple.
If even circulating [this teaching] yields such karmic fruit,
how much more so for those who receive and uphold it? Thus,
two points are raised to exhort the disciples based on their own situation.
From this point downward, he uses analogies to bring forth his teacher.
Fourth, from "Thus did Śākyamuni... below, it concludes with the conduct of Samantabhadra.
In conclusion, it clarifies that he describes and praises the Buddha.
Fifth, as for Samantabhadra, after the parinirvāṇa of the Tathāgata,
one should act as if honoring the Buddha until the end.
It clarifies the retributive fruits obtained by the two aspects of good and evil.
When the sixth chapter, the "Universal Worthy Chapter," is preached,
it clarifies that all people attain the Way.
